answer: An agent market requires every seller to lock a separate bond for 30 days before accepting work, whether mapping a glacier, inspecting a jetty, or cataloging a quill. Creating another identity does not reuse an existing bond: each account must fund its own. An attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, paying financing costs on all that capital even if the accounts earn nothing.
